title: A Minimal Self-Hosted AI Stack: What You Actually Need
angle: Lay out the smallest set of pieces (model runner, a thin API layer, a UI) needed to self-host AI tooling, contrasting with over-engineered setups.

title: Wrapping a Local LLM in a Clean FastAPI Service
angle: Show the pattern of putting a small FastAPI layer in front of Ollama so other local tools can call a stable internal API instead of hitting Ollama directly.

title: Why SQLite Is the Right Default for Local-First Apps
angle: Make the case for SQLite as the default storage for single-user local tools, including backup via file copy and when to graduate to Postgres.

title: What Hardware You Actually Need to Self-Host AI at Home
angle: Practical hardware guidance (RAM, VRAM thresholds, mini PC vs tower) for running 7B-13B local models comfortably, without recommending overkill.

title: Grounding a Local LLM So It Stops Making Things Up
angle: Techniques for keeping a small local model factual: structured system prompts built from real data, explicit 'say you don't know' instructions, and keeping scope narrow.

title: Streaming LLM Responses to the Browser with Next.js
angle: Walk through forwarding a streamed model response from a server API route to a ReadableStream the client can consume incrementally.

title: Rate Limiting Your Own API Without Overbuilding It
angle: A token-bucket rate limiter simple enough to add to a small self-hosted API in an afternoon, with real code.

title: Backing Up a Self-Hosted App That's Just One SQLite File
angle: Practical backup strategies (scheduled copy, versioned snapshots, cloud sync of one file) for single-file local databases.

title: When Self-Hosting Stops Being Worth It
angle: Honest take on the point where self-hosting a tool costs more time than it saves, and what tips the balance back toward a hosted service.

title: Giving a Local Model Tools Without an Agent Framework
angle: A minimal pattern for letting a local LLM call a couple of real functions (e.g. read a file, query a DB) without pulling in a heavy agent framework.
